desc: At the Reconfigurable Robotics Lab we focus on the design, actuation, fabrication, and control of unique robotic systems. The research in our lab is committed to inventing interactive robotic systems with novel fabrication techniques and integration processes that push the limits of mechanical properties. These efforts enable us to create soft, reconfigurable, and interactive robots that are highly conscious of the environment and have extensive applications in wearable technology, medical/rehabilitation systems, and personal robots. Reconfigurable Robogami modules for human augmentation Origami-inspired, lightweight modules configure to wearable robotic arms that adapt seamlessly and safely to various environments and tasks. Immersive Multi-modal Full-Body Feedback for Tangible Experiences Origami-inspired Dynamic Experience Platform that delivers whole-body feedback by translating audiovisual content into motion, and recreating real-world kinetic experience, making digital content immersive and tangible. Self-Assembling Modular Origami Robots A swarm of identical triangular origami modules that locate each other, assemble themselves into a requested shape with no central controller, and accept plug-in capability cores, so one set of hardware becomes whatever robot the mission needs. Surface-Based Manipulation A team of reconfigurable modular robots, each ending in a simple flat plate, moves, flips, and reorients objects across their surfaces—manipulating without ever grasping. Digits: Reconfigurable Haptic Feedback Digits is a reconfigurable haptic interface composed of modular pneumatic actuators that can be arranged in different configurations to render multimodal haptic feedback with precise pressure control. Viscous Airflow Reconfiguration System Predictive fluidic-network framework that transforms a small number of shared pneumatic inputs into dynamically reprogrammable spatiotemporal actuation fields. SORI: a softness rendering interface SORI is a reconfigurable haptic display that decouples contact area and force on human fingertips, with model-based softness cue estimation to render a personalized experience with both virtual and real-world objects.

desc: The Operating Room X (OR-X) is an open-access center for surgical research and training, providing a highly realistic environment in which new technologies and procedures can be developed, tested, and validated under clinically relevant conditions. As a lighthouse for surgical innovation and part of the SERI Roadmap of Research Infrastructures, the OR-X helps bridge the gap between technological development and clinical application. Its 1,185 m² facility combines a fully equipped operating room with a dedicated skills lab, creating flexible and reproducible conditions for research across all surgical disciplines. This infrastructure allows technologies such as surgical robotics, navigation, imaging, AI, tracking, and data-driven solutions to be integrated directly into realistic surgical workflows and evaluated in a controlled setting. By bringing clinical expertise, engineering, and research together in one shared environment, the OR-X enables close collaboration between medical professionals, researchers, technology developers, and industry partners. In doing so, it supports the development and translation of new solutions that can help shape the future of surgery. Learn more by watching our video here . Compliant endoscope and cannula manipulator for uniportal surgery Uniportal endoscopic spine surgery is ergonomically demanding: the surgeon controls both endoscope and cannula through a single corridor with one hand, adjusting the view while actively manipulating tissue. Existing robotic systems are built for multiport soft-tissue procedures and do not address the constraints of uniportal interventions or active cannula manipulation. This work presents a robotic holder designed for uniportal interventions that can operate autonomously or in collaboration with surgeons or possibly external robotic systems (co-robotics). It addresses both the ergonomic limitations of hand-held instruments and the lack of cannula manipulation in existing robotic systems. Visuo-haptic Digital Twin Of Real Surgeries For Training In this project we create an immersive visuo-haptic environment for surgical training. The operating room and patient are dynamically reconstructed in 3D and presented in Virtual- or Augmented Reality, providing the trainee a learning environment from real data. The trainee can train the presented surgery step, while receiving haptic feedback, as well as qualitative and quantitative feedback on their performance. Watch the demo video here .
